title: How we optimized our workflows and overcame GitHub Actions limitations
gist: The llama.cpp team (ggml-org) describes how they outgrew GitHub Actions' free-plan limits (10GB cache, 20 concurrent runners) for a 100+ job CI, and fixed it by splitting PR vs master workflows, moving ccache data to Hugging Face Buckets, and offloading most Linux x64 jobs to Hugging Face Jobs via the jobs-actions dispatcher — a case study that doubles as Hugging Face pushing into CI compute and storage.

insights.claim: llama.cpp received 3,181 pull requests between August and October 2026 (about 35 per day) and merged 1,802 of them.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Signals intense developer engagement in local/open-source LLM inference — a leading indicator for on-device AI adoption.
insights.quote: the project received 3,181 pull requests (about 35 per day) and merged 1,802 of them.

insights.claim: A complete llama.cpp CI run has 100+ jobs across many hardware backends, many taking up to ~30 minutes, plus pre-release builds for almost every merged PR that can take a few hours.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Multi-backend support (CUDA, HIP, MUSA) imposes heavy build costs — hardware diversity in local AI has real maintenance overhead.

insights.claim: llama.cpp's CUDA backend relies on many C++ templates and is built for CUDA, HIP and MUSA backends across multiple hardware architectures, making builds slow without cached object files.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: llama.cpp actively supports AMD (HIP) and Moore Threads (MUSA) alongside Nvidia CUDA — open-source tooling is broadening non-Nvidia GPU viability.

insights.claim: GitHub Actions caps cache for free public repos at 10GB with least-recently-used eviction, which forced llama.cpp jobs to recompile when their ccache entries were evicted.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Large open-source projects outgrow GitHub's free tier — an opening for alternative CI compute/storage vendors.
insights.quote: The total available cache for free, public Github repos is limited to 10GB.

insights.claim: GitHub's free plan limits the ggml-org organization to 20 concurrent GitHub-hosted jobs, at most five of them macOS, so a 100+ job CI run leaves many jobs waiting for runners.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Runner concurrency, not compute speed, is the bottleneck for big OSS CI — monetizable pain point for CI providers.
insights.quote: with 20 concurrent GitHub-hosted jobs across the organization, including at most five macOS jobs within that total.

themes.theme: Hugging Face Buckets as cache store

insights.claim: llama.cpp moved non-release ccache data from GitHub Actions Cache to Hugging Face Buckets: master builds upload a cache snapshot and PR builds download it, freeing GitHub cache space for release builds.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Hugging Face is expanding beyond model hosting into general developer storage infrastructure, competing with S3-type services.
insights.locator: Store compiler caches in Hugging Face Buckets

insights.claim: Hugging Face Buckets is an S3-like storage service backed by Xet with upload/download-level deduplication, which Hugging Face positions as faster and cheaper storage.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Dedup-backed storage is Hugging Face's wedge into commodity object storage — watch adoption vs AWS S3.
insights.quote: Hugging Face Buckets is an S3-like storage service backed by Xet, with deduplication on upload/download level
insights.locator: Store compiler caches in Hugging Face Buckets

insights.claim: Shared bucket storage was a prerequisite for moving llama.cpp CI to ephemeral cloud runners, because each new runner can fetch its build cache without relying on a previous runner's persistent disk.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Storage and compute products reinforce each other — Hugging Face bundling Buckets with Jobs increases platform lock-in.
insights.quote: Bucket storage was necessary before this move.
insights.locator: Run Linux x64 jobs on Hugging Face Jobs

themes.theme: Hugging Face Jobs as CI runners

insights.claim: llama.cpp offloaded most Linux x64 CI jobs from GitHub-hosted and some self-hosted runners to Hugging Face Jobs, cloud CPU/GPU instances billed per instance uptime.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Marquee OSS project as reference customer for Hugging Face's compute business — a new revenue line beyond the Hub.
insights.quote: jobs are charged per uptime of the instance
insights.locator: Run Linux x64 jobs on Hugging Face Jobs

insights.claim: Hugging Face's jobs-actions keeps GitHub Actions as orchestrator: runner labels like hf-jobs-cpu-upgrade or hf-jobs-t4-small trigger a webhook to a dispatcher Space, which mints a short-lived registration token and boots an ephemeral GitHub runner on matching Hugging Face hardware, streaming logs back to GitHub.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Low-friction 'bring your own runner' integration lets Hugging Face capture CI compute spend without displacing GitHub — easy adoption path.
insights.quote: Rather than replacing GitHub Actions as our primary workflow orchestrator, jobs-actions functions as a lightweight dispatcher and bridge.
insights.locator: Running GitHub Actions with Hugging Face Jobs

insights.claim: llama.cpp also cut per-PR CI work by selecting jobs based on the diff, while keeping the complete CI job set for pushes to master.
insights.speaker: Sigbjørn Skjæret
insights.so_what: Diff-based test selection is a standard cost lever for large repos facing runner scarcity.
